hero.subtitle: When a diagnosis or treatment goes wrong at a Colusa County clinic or hospital, the aftermath can be confusing and isolating. We can help you understand your options at no cost. Our team handles medical malpractice claims in this area.

about.title: Colusa Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Colusa is a small community of under 6,000 people, and many residents rely on a limited number of local clinics and one regional hospital system for care. When something goes wrong — a missed diagnosis, a surgical mistake, a medication error — patients here often have fewer nearby alternatives and may feel unsure about questioning a provider they know personally. California law recognizes that medical errors happen and gives injured patients a path to seek accountability, but medical malpractice cases carry strict rules: a short window to act, a required pre-suit notice, and the need for a qualified medical expert to review the care you received. A bad result by itself doesn't prove malpractice; the question is whether the provider deviated from the accepted standard of care. We evaluate these claims and work on contingency, meaning there's no upfront cost to find out where you stand.

items.title: Understanding California's Notice Requirement
items.desc: California requires a 90-day pre-suit notice to the provider before a malpractice lawsuit can be filed. We can help make sure this step is handled correctly and on time.

items.title: Navigating a Short, Strict Timeline
items.desc: Medical malpractice claims generally must be filed within one year of discovering the injury, and no more than three years from when it occurred. Missing these deadlines can end a claim before it starts.

items.title: Working With Required Medical Experts
items.desc: California law almost always requires a qualified medical expert to support a malpractice claim. We can help connect your case with the right kind of medical review.

items.question: Is a bad medical outcome automatically malpractice?
items.answer: No. California law recognizes that not every poor result is caused by a provider's error. Malpractice requires showing that a provider's care fell below the accepted medical standard, which is why an expert medical review is almost always part of these claims.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim in Colusa County?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from when you discover the injury, and no more than three years from when it happened, whichever comes first. Because Colusa has limited local providers, gathering records and expert opinions can take time, so it helps to start early.

items.question: What does California's damages cap mean for my case?
items.answer: California law places a cap on non-economic damages — such as pain and suffering — in medical malpractice cases, though that cap increases each year under current law. We can explain how this applies to your specific situation.

items.question: Do you charge anything to get started?
items.answer: No. We offer a free consultation, and we typically work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation.
